extracted.intended_audience: community water system operators, small and non-transient non-community water systems, and State drinking water regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements in 40 CFR Part 141 concerning lead monitoring, public education, sampling, reporting, small-system compliance flexibility (POU devices or plumbing replacement), point-of-entry device use, recordkeeping, disinfectant/disinfection byproduct controls, and approved analytical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual report contents for schools/child care
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning one year after the compliance date in §141.80(a)(3), a community water system must send an annual report to the State by January 30 for the previous year's activity that includes specific certifications and information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must include: (i) certification of good faith effort to identify schools and child care facilities (may include reviewing customer records and requesting lists); (ii) certification that health-risk information was delivered to schools/child care per §141.92(c)(1); (iii)-(v) certifications about completion of notification and sampling requirements in the first five years and thereafter (with lists and counts described in (iii)(A)-(E)); and (vi) certification that sampling results were provided to schools, child care facilities, and local and State health departments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good faith effort to identify schools and child care facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification that the water system made a good faith effort to identify schools and child care facilities in accordance with §141.92(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good faith effort may include reviewing customer records and requesting lists from the State or other licensing agencies; if changes occur, submit an updated list at least once every five years per §141.92(b)(2); if no changes, certify no changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver public-education materials to schools/child care
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification that the water system has delivered information about health risks from lead in drinking water to the schools and child care facilities they serve in accordance with §141.92(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public education must be consistent with content requirements of §141.85(a)(1)(ii)-(iv) and (vi) and may reference EPA's 3Ts Toolkit (EPA-815-B-18-007) or subsequent guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual listing and counts for sampled/non-responsive/declined facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: During the first five years after the compliance date, report must include number and names of schools/child care facilities served, sampled in the previous year, declined sampling, did not respond to outreach, and information about outreach attempts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These correspond to items (iii)(A)-(E) and must be included in the annual report to the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting tap sampling results for POU option
rubrics_metrics.description: Small systems using the point-of-use (POU) device option must report results from tap sampling required under §141.93(c)(1)(iv) no later than 10 days after the end of the tap sampling period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If corrective action is not completed within 30 days of a POU sample exceeding 0.010 mg/L, system must provide documentation to the State within 30 days explaining why it was unable to correct the issue. Systems must provide documentation to certify maintenance of POU devices unless waived by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of replacement for small-system plumbing option
rubrics_metrics.description: Small water systems implementing the option to replace all lead-bearing plumbing under §141.93(c)(2) must provide certification to the State that all lead-bearing material has been replaced on the schedule established by the State, within one year of designation of the option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification submitted to State in accordance with §141.90(j)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: Any system subject to the requirements of this subpart shall retain on its premises original records of all sampling data and analyses, reports, surveys, letters, evaluations, schedules, State determinations, and any other information required by §§141.81–141.88, 141.90, 141.92, and 141.93.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each water system shall retain the records required by this section for no fewer than 12 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability exception for newer construction and plumbing
rubrics_metrics.description: Community water systems need not conduct public education and lead monitoring at schools/child care facilities that were constructed or had full plumbing replacement on or after January 1, 2014 (or date State adopted lead-free standard) and are not served by a lead, a galvanized requiring replacement, or an unknown service line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also does not apply to schools/child care facilities regulated as a public water system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compile and submit list of schools and child care facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: All community water systems must compile a list of schools and child care facilities they serve that meet the criteria of applicability and submit the list to the State in accordance with §141.90(i)(1) by the compliance date in §141.80(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within five years after the compliance date and at least once every five-year period after, systems must either certify in writing there have been no changes or submit a revised list per §141.90(i)(3)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual contact and content of public education to schools/child care
rubrics_metrics.description: At least once a year beginning with the compliance date, community water systems must contact all identified schools and child care facilities to provide information about health risks from lead in drinking water consistent with §141.85(a)(1)(ii)-(iv) and (vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within first five years, notices to elementary schools/child care must include a proposed sampling schedule and EPA's 3Ts Toolkit information; secondary schools must be notified at least once a year that they are eligible for sampling on request and be given information on how to request sampling and EPA 3Ts guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thirty-day pre-sampling instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Thirty days prior to any sampling event, community water systems must provide schools and child care facilities with instructions to identify outlets for lead sampling and prepare for a sampling event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps facility staff identify which outlets will be sampled and preparation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling frequency for elementary schools and child care facilities (first five years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the first five years following the compliance date, community water systems must collect samples from at least 20 percent of the total elementary schools served per year and at least 20 percent of the total child care facilities served per year (or alternative State-approved schedule) until all identified facilities have been sampled once or have declined or been non-responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems may count refusals or non-responses as part of the 20%; non-responsive may be considered after at least two outreach attempts; documentation of refusals/non-responses must be provided to the State per §141.90(i)(3)(iii)(D) and (E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling frequency starting sixth year for elementary schools/child care
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting with the sixth year after the compliance date, community water systems must conduct sampling when requested by an elementary school or child care facility but are not required to sample more than 20% of the facilities in any given year nor an individual facility more than once in any five-year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-time inclusions in updated lists require outreach prior to sampling as specified in §141.92(c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling frequency for secondary schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting with the compliance date, community water systems must conduct sampling for secondary schools when requested; systems are not required to sample more than 20% of secondary schools in any year nor any single secondary school more than once in any five-year period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondary schools must be notified annually they are eligible for sampling on request and given instructions on how to request sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead sampling protocol: number and types of samples/outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Community water systems must collect five samples per school and two samples per child care facility at outlets typically used to provide water for human consumption (except as provided in specified exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For schools: two drinking water fountains, one kitchen faucet used for drinking/cooking, one classroom faucet or other outlet used for human consumption, and one nurse's office faucet, as available. For child care: one drinking fountain and one of either a kitchen faucet used for drinking/cooking or one classroom faucet. If fewer outlets exist, sample all; may sample outlets with POU devices only in specific circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling protocol: first draw, volume, stagnation time, analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Each lead sample must be a first draw sample, 250 mL in volume; the water must have remained stationary in the building plumbing for at least 8 but no more than 18 hours; and samples must be analyzed using acidification and the corresponding analytical methods in §141.89.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Samples must be collected by system staff, school/child care staff, or other appropriately trained individuals in accordance with the protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may collect samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Community water system, school, or child care facility staff, or other appropriately trained individuals must collect samples in accordance with the sampling protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training and adherence to specified protocol (first draw, volume, stagnation, sample handling, analytical methods) are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of sampling results timing and recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Community water systems must provide sampling results, regardless of lead concentration, as soon as practicable but no later than 30 days after receipt of the results to: (i) the sampled school or child care facility with info about remediation options; (ii) the local and State health department; and (iii) the State per §141.90(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information about potential remediation options should be consistent with EPA's 3Ts Toolkit or subsequent guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: State waiver/exemption criteria for alternative sampling programs
rubrics_metrics.description: If schools/child care facilities are sampled under a State or local law/program, the State may exempt community water systems from sampling requirements by issuing a written waiver if the alternative program meets specific frequency and protocol requirements or is accompanied by remedial actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver conditions include: alternative sampling that meets frequency and protocol in §141.92(d) & (e) and protocol in (f); or meeting frequency and protocol except sample size/stagnation when sampling is conducted in addition to remediation actions (disconnect affected fixtures, replace fixtures with lead-free, install/maintain certified POU devices); or other specified conditions. Duration cannot exceed the covered sampling period and expires after any 12-month period without required sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative compliance eligibility for small systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Small community water systems (serving ≤3,300) and non-transient non-community systems that exceed the lead action level but not the copper action level may elect to use §141.93 flexibility in lieu of corrosion control if approved by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not available where State has primacy and has not adopted consistent regulations; approval, recommendations, and schedules involve State review and potential designation of alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-system requirement to evaluate corrosion control and water quality parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems electing the flexibility must collect water quality parameters per §141.87 and, if not re-optimized/installed OCCT, evaluate compliance options and corrosion control treatment options under §141.81(d) or (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems with corrosion control must continue to operate/maintain optimal treatment until State determines otherwise and may need to meet additional State requirements before implementing alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline for system recommendation and State decision on alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: The system must make a compliance option recommendation to the State within six months of the end of the tap sampling period in which the lead action level exceedance occurred; the State has six months to approve or disapprove.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If State disapproves, it may designate another compliance alternative; if no designation, the system must comply with otherwise applicable corrosion control treatment requirements and follow schedules in §141.81.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative: POU device installation coverage and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system electing the POU device option must install, maintain, and monitor POU devices in each household and each building served by the system on a State-specified schedule: for community systems, a minimum of one POU per household and at every tap used for cooking/drinking in non-residential buildings not to exceed one year after State approval; for non-transient non-community systems, provide a POU to every tap used for cooking/drinking not to exceed three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POU devices must be independently certified to relevant ANSI standards, maintained per manufacturer or State schedule, equipped with mechanical warnings for operational problems, and documented to the State unless waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: POU device monitoring, sample type, and performance standard
rubrics_metrics.description: POU devices must be monitored such that one-third of devices are monitored each year and all devices monitored within a three-year cycle. First liter tap samples must be taken after water passes through the POU device, be one liter in volume, and have at least a 6-hour stagnation time. All samples must be at or below 0.010 mg/L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must report results no later than 10 days after end of tap sampling period; if a sample exceeds 0.010 mg/L, notify persons served/building management within one business day of receiving results; document and take corrective action at each site within 30 days or provide State documentation explaining delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education content, timing, and delivery for POU option
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems approved to implement POU devices must provide public education materials informing users how to properly use POU devices to maximize effectiveness; materials must meet §141.85(a)(1)(ii)-(iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education must be provided at time of POU device delivery and delivered in person, by mail, or by another State-approved method to persons at locations where devices were delivered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation and maintenance obligation while using POU option
rubrics_metrics.description: The water system must operate and maintain the POU devices even if the system is at or below the action level in future monitoring periods until the system receives State approval to select another compliance option or to follow §141.81(d) or (e) and has fully implemented it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued M&R ensures ongoing protection until a new approved strategy is in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative: replacement of lead-bearing plumbing — scope and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: A water system that controls all plumbing and is not served by lead/galvanized/unknown service lines may elect to replace all plumbing that does not meet the definition of 'lead free' in section 1417 on a State-established schedule not to exceed one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Water systems must provide certification to the State that all lead-bearing material has been replaced in accordance with §141.90(j)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-of-entry devices: state-approved monitoring plan and equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems may use point-of-entry devices to comply with MCLs only if they develop and obtain State approval for a monitoring plan before installation; under the plan, point-of-entry devices must provide health protection equivalent to central water treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent means meeting all national primary drinking water regulations and producing water of acceptable quality similar to well-operated central treatment; monitoring must include VOCs, total flow treated, and mechanical condition observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-of-entry devices: design review, certification, and microbiological safety
rubrics_metrics.description: States must require adequate certification of performance, field testing, and, if not included in certification, a rigorous engineering design review of point-of-entry devices; design/application must consider potential increases in heterotrophic bacteria and may require backwashing, post-contactor disinfection, and HPC monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures microbiological safety is not compromised when using activated carbon or similar media; State must assure adequate controls, testing, and maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point-of-entry devices: coverage and conveyance of responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Every building connected to the system must have a point-of-entry device installed, maintained, and adequately monitored; the State must be assured every building is subject to treatment/monitoring and that the rights/responsibilities of the public water system customer convey with title upon sale of property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents gaps in protection and ensures responsibilities persist through property transfers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of bottled water
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems shall not use bottled water to achieve compliance with an MCL; bottled water may be used on a temporary basis to avoid unreasonable risk to health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bottled water is explicitly disallowed as a long-term compliance method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator qualification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each CWS and NTNCWS regulated under Subpart L must be operated by qualified personnel who meet State-specified requirements and are included in a State register of qualified operators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures systems adding disinfectants are run by trained/registered operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of disinfectant residuals during emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding MRDLs, systems may increase residual disinfectant levels of chlorine or chloramines (but not chlorine dioxide) in the distribution system to a level and for a time necessary to protect public health to address specific microbiological contamination events (e.g., line breaks, storm run-off, source contamination, cross-connections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows temporary operational flexibility for public-health protective actions; chlorine dioxide excluded from this temporary increase authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical methods: use only approved or EPA-equivalent methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must use only the analytical methods specified in §141.131, or their equivalent as approved by EPA, to demonstrate compliance with Subpart L and Subparts U and V; incorporated methods are effective for compliance monitoring as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific EPA, Standard Methods, and ASTM methods for various analytes (TTHM, HAA5, bromate, chlorite, etc.), references to method documents and availability, and footnotes specifying limitations (e.g., extraction within 14 days, IC/ICP-MS for bromate reduced-monitoring eligibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection byproduct methods and special requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved analytical methods for disinfection byproduct compliance monitoring are specified (e.g., EPA Methods 502.2, 524.2, 551.1, 552.1/2/3, Standard Methods, ASTM), with method-specific notes and footnotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes clarify method-specific requirements such as sample extraction timelines, use of IC/ICP-MS for bromate under certain conditions, and method equivalence for particular analytes. Systems must follow cited method editions or IBR-approved versions.
